This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER
This is the first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant is in custody since 30.09.2022 in connection with Crime No.400/2022 registered at Police Station Rajpur, District Barwani (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 376, 376(2)(N), 506 of the Indian Penal Code of 1860 read with Section 3/4 and 5/6 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act.

As per prosecution story, minor prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S. Rajpur, Dist. Barwani by stating that present applicant repeatedly committed sexual assault on her by threatening to kill her and after that she get pregnant.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 30.09.2022.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix (PW-1), her mother (PW-2) and brother (PW-3) have been examined before the trial Court.
They all have turned hostile and have not supported the prosecution story.
Applicant is permanent resident of Barwani district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that present applicant be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has been turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story, she has categorically stated in her statement that present applicant Rashid neither abducted nor committed any rape upon her, her mother (PW-2) and brother (PW-3) have also deposed in the same manner, prosecutrix has stated in her statement that one Rahul committed some wrong act with her and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In view of the above, without commenting on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, the application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Rahid vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139243968/
